name: acme
source: The ACME example, docs/reference/examples/acme. The plan is the JSON form of acme.obk.yaml that the plan decoder and encoder contracts check against it. The document is acme.md in this folder, written by hand from the rules in this contract, because the document in the docs folder cannot be produced by one set of rules. Decisions to know, first item, lists the differences.

name: empty-plan
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Title, Review line, Gap table. A plan with no sections and no answers.

name: title-organization-only
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Title, Review line. Decisions to know, title forms. The date and the template set differ from the other cases.

name: title-team-only
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Title. A deferred organization counts as absent.

name: title-empty-text
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Title. Empty text counts as absent.

name: minimal-section
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Sections. A section with only the required fields has no footer and no gaps. Docs: domain model, Section.

name: prose-as-held
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Prose is written as held. Docs: schema README, prose fields hold Markdown.

name: footers
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Footer, and the order of sections from the section selector. The footer lines come from the ACME document.

name: reading-order
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Sections come in the selector's order, with no heading for a timing. Docs: ordering. The plan is the one a section after another section needs.

name: gaps-deferred
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Gap table. Docs: variables, deferred answers. The Text deferred is a plain string and is no gap.

name: gaps-unanswered
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Gap table. Rows follow the resolver's problems, a section with no owner leaves the cell empty, and a variable with no description shows its name.

name: gap-timings
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Footer, Gap table. The five timing names from the schema reference, ordering, plus an omitted timing.

name: onboarding-blank
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Markdown. Docs: variables, phase onboarding shows a blank. The ACME document wraps the blank in backticks.

name: people-list
source: Hand-written. Docs: variables, person. The ACME document shows a person list as a sentence. The addresses use the reserved example domain.

name: steps-all-fields
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Steps. Docs: steps, every field of a step and a check.

name: inactive-section
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Sections. Docs: optional sections, only active sections appear. The ACME plan's design section is the model.

name: table-cell-escaping
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Markdown, table cells.

name: switched-off-section
source: Hand-written. 0050: the section selector is active when its switch is on, and a section with enabled false is off. Contract rule: Sections, a section that is not active is not in the document and its gaps are not in the table. A section with enabled true is on. The switched-off section declares an unanswered variable that its text uses, so a gap would show if it were resolved.

name: switch-clause-condition
source: Hand-written. 0050: a section clause in includeIf holds when the named section's switch equals enabled, and tests the switch only. Contract rule: Sections. A section whose includeIf needs a switched-off section to be on is left out, with its gaps, and one that needs it to be off is written. A section that needs an inactive section whose switch is on is written, because the clause does not read the other section's includeIf.

name: enabled-variable
source: Hand-written. 0050: a variable named enabled is no longer the toggle, it is an ordinary variable. Contract rule: Sections and the resolver contract. A section whose variable enabled is answered false stays in the document and the answer is written as text. The same name unanswered is a gap like any other.

name: sub-sections
source: Hand-written. 0070 and the selector contract, Order: a sub-section comes after its parent and its earlier siblings' subtrees, depth first, siblings by effective timing (own, or the parent's), then after, then id, and no root crosses a timing line. Contract rule: Sections, heading level. The sub-section with no timing has no When line and a gap row of Anytime, because the section is written as held. The plan lists the sections out of order. Among the siblings, the id order differs from the timing order, and the sub-section with no timing sorts by its parent's.

name: inactive-parent
source: Hand-written. 0070: a sub-section is active only if its parent is active, at any depth, by the parent's own includeIf and switch. Contract rule: Sections. A sub-section whose own switch is true under a switched-off parent is left out with its gaps, and so is the grandchild of a switched-off sub-section and of an excluded parent. A sub-section of an active parent stays.

name: depth-cap
source: Hand-written. 0070 and the brief: the heading is 2 plus the depth of the section in the plan, and never deeper than six. Contract rule: Sections. The chain runs from depth zero to depth seven.
